```{python}
        a_brake,
        j_brake,
        AISLE.delta_loc + AISLE.eps_track,
        AISLE.delta_margin,
    ).to(meter / second)
    ceil_ool = calc_scurve_max_permitted_velocity(
        d_clear,
        tau_delay + t_ool,
        a_brake,
        j_brake,
        AISLE.delta_loc + AISLE.eps_track,
        AISLE.delta_margin,
    ).to(meter / second)

    # ┌── 3. GUARD (Invariants) ───────────────────────────────────────────
    check(abs(spare.magnitude - 131.01) < 5e-3, f"spare margin at the aisle speed: {spare}")
    check(abs(t_latest.magnitude - 100.775) < 5e-3, f"T_latest at the aisle speed: {t_latest}")
    check(abs(ceil_in.magnitude - 0.8362) < 5e-5, f"in-loop takeover ceiling: {ceil_in}")
    check(abs(ceil_ool.magnitude - 0.1911) < 5e-5, f"out-of-loop takeover ceiling: {ceil_ool}")
    check(v_in < ceil_in and v_ool < ceil_ool, "The chosen request speeds must sit under their ceilings.")
    check(abs(t_latest_in.magnitude - 751.608) < 5e-3, f"T_latest at the in-loop slow-down: {t_latest_in}")

    # ┌── 4. OUTPUT (Formatting) ──────────────────────────────────────────
    v_str = fmt_velocity(v, unit=meter / second, precision=1)
    spare_str = fmt_length(spare, unit=millimeter, precision=1)
    t_latest_str = fmt_latency(t_latest, unit=millisecond, precision=1)
    v_in_str = fmt_velocity(v_in, unit=meter / second, precision=2)
    v_ool_str = fmt_velocity(v_ool, unit=meter / second, precision=2)
    t_in_str = fmt_latency(t_in, unit=millisecond, precision=0)
    t_ool_str = fmt_latency(t_ool, unit=second, precision=1)
    ceil_in_str = fmt_velocity(ceil_in, unit=meter / second, precision=2)
    ceil_ool_str = fmt_velocity(ceil_ool, unit=meter / second, precision=2)
    t_latest_in_str = fmt_latency(t_latest_in, unit=millisecond, precision=1)
```

Supervisory intervention transfers the right to propose, never the right to admit. A capability matrix grants each authenticated role named operations on named actuator channels, each with a preemption tier and a clearance-derived deadline, while the enforcer checks every command from every source against the same physical envelope. Enforcement changes a proposal and leaves the proposer in place; intervention changes the proposer and leaves the check in place, and the machine needs both.

A takeover is a delay inserted before braking on a moving machine, so it is priced in the stopping budget rather than in the user interface. At the `{python} InterventionSummaryWaiting.v_str` aisle speed the subtotal before dispatch-to-admission travel leaves `{python} InterventionSummaryWaiting.spare_str`, a waiting window of `{python} InterventionSummaryWaiting.t_latest_str`, and only `{python} InterventionAdmissionAllocation.left_aisle_str` once the `{python} InterventionAdmissionAllocation.delta_da_str` dispatch-to-admission allocation of @sec-placement-dispatch-admission is charged. Sourced human responses of `{python} InterventionSummaryWaiting.t_in_str` in the loop and `{python} InterventionSummaryWaiting.t_ool_str` out of it cap the request speed at `{python} InterventionSummaryWaiting.ceil_in_str` and `{python} InterventionSummaryWaiting.ceil_ool_str` before that charge, and no brake, however strong, admits the aisle speed, because the waiting term rather than the braking term spends the clearance. The design therefore slows to `{python} InterventionSummaryWaiting.v_in_str` before an anticipated in-loop request, crawls at `{python} InterventionSummaryWaiting.v_ool_str` or stops first before an out-of-loop one, and answers a newly discovered hazard with its own local stop. None of these speeds qualifies until loaded measurements confirm the allocation and the braking premises.

Authority is bounded and moved by mechanisms that never wait on the network. Execution leases on the safety microcontroller's clock, the autonomous chunk lease and the `{python} InterventionTimeoutBudget.manual_lease_str` manual lease, revoke a silent proposer and select the fallback that matches the machine's state. A four-phase handshake commits ownership on one control tick for an explicit channel mask, the enforcer remains the only writer to the actuators, and every timer that expires leads to a defined state. Authentication keeps forged commands out of admission, but only a rate limiter ahead of the verifier keeps forged traffic from delaying a genuine veto, and hardwired protective inputs bypass both.

Changing the proposer does not change the physics of the command. A fixed-endpoint $\Glyph{C}^2$ smoothstep\index{C2 bumpless transfer ramp@$\Glyph{C}^2$ bumpless authority transfer ramp} bounds the command rate between latched endpoints, but it spends clearance. The base window is `{python} InterventionBlendBudget.T_budget_str` at every speed because the jerk bound belongs to the loaded base, and at the `{python} InterventionBlendBudget.v0_str` request speed no braking blend fits the clearance that remains. Within the stated one-dimensional stopping model and boundary conditions, no smoothed braking under the same bounds beats the resident profile, so the base receives the resident stop while the arm blends over `{python} InterventionBlendBudget.arm_budget_str`.

The authority record turns every handover into evidence. It binds the sealed static manifest to per-tick evidence tuples that record who held each channel and what was proposed, admitted, and dispatched alongside independent measurements of the response, chains them against tampering, and declares every gap. It draws its fallback rungs from the enforcement record and its declared timing bounds from the placement record, whose loaded measurements are still to come. The same ownership timestamps serve two readers. An investigator can reconstruct an incident from them, provided independent current, encoder, and contact measurements confirm what the commands did, and a learner can apply this chapter's conservative four-interval direct-imitation mask, under which only validated, stabilized human recovery supplies post-takeover demonstration targets. Other learning objectives use the same provenance with different eligibility rules (@tbl-14-intervention-learning).

@Tbl-14-key-equations summarizes the governing quantitative relations for supervisory intervention, detailing the specific operational or physical quantity bounded by each equation.

| Equation                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | What it bounds or decides                                                                       | Derived in                                                            |
|:------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|:------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|:----------------------------------------------------------------------|
| $\SupervisoryTakeoverLatency = \OperatorSensoryTime + \OperatorCognitiveTime + \OperatorMotorTime + \ConsoleCommunicationTime$                                                                                                                        | The takeover delay a person and a console add before any command changes                        | @eq-intervention-reaction-floor                                       |
| $\SpeedAtDetection(\ExternalWait + \PrebrakeDelay) + \ResidentStopDistance(\SpeedAtDetection) + \FixedClearanceAllowance \le \ClearDistance$                                                                                                          | Whether the machine can still stop after waiting $\ExternalWait$ at speed $\SpeedAtDetection$   | @eq-intervention-stopping-inequality                                  |
| $\FallbackDeadline = (\ClearDistance - \FixedClearanceAllowance - \ResidentStopDistance(\SpeedAtDetection))/\SpeedAtDetection - \PrebrakeDelay$                                                                                                       | The latest fallback dispatch after a handover request; a fixed timeout is clipped to it         | @eq-intervention-latest-fallback                                      |
| $\SpeedBound = \CredibleBrakingDeceleration\bigl[\sqrt{\FullSpeedTravelTime^2 + 2(\ClearDistance-\FixedClearanceAllowance)/\CredibleBrakingDeceleration} - \FullSpeedTravelTime\bigr]$                                                                | The highest speed at which a takeover with delay $\SupervisoryTakeoverLatency$ may be requested | @eq-intervention-speed-ceiling                                        |
| $\TimeInstant - \LeaseRefreshInstant < \ChunkLease$ or $\ManualLease$                                                                                                                                                                                 | Whether a proposer still holds authority; expiry invokes the validated local response           | @eq-intervention-lease-age                                            |
| $\BumplessTransferBlend(\BumplessTransferProgress) = 10\BumplessTransferProgress^3 - 15\BumplessTransferProgress^4 + 6\BumplessTransferProgress^5$ with $\BlendingTransitionWindow \ge 1.875\,\lVert \FiniteChange \ControlCommand \rVert/\JerkLimit$ | The minimum window within the fixed-endpoint quintic family under the stated rate ceiling       | @eq-intervention-quintic-smoothstep and @eq-intervention-blend-window |
| $\LossFunction = \mathbb{E}\bigl[\sum_k \CausalInterventionMask(\ControlSampleIndex)\,\ell(\Policy(\MechanicalPlantState_k), \ImitationTargetCommand(\ControlSampleIndex))\bigr]$                                                                     | Which logged samples train the next policy, and with which target                               | @eq-intervention-causal-masking-loss                                  |

: **Key equations of supervisory intervention**: Each equation fixes one quantity a takeover design must declare. The kinematic relations assume the jerk-limited resident stop and a constant speed while the machine waits; the ceiling's closed form holds only above $\CredibleBrakingDeceleration^2/\JerkLimit$. The delays inside them must be measured on the site's operators, console, and link. {#tbl-14-key-equations tbl-colwidths="[44,40,16]"}

::: {.callout-takeaways title="Supervisory intervention and authority bounds"}
* **State-dependent fallback and monotonic leases:** Bind each proposer to an explicit, mode-specific lease and stopping reserve. Lease expiry invokes the validated local fallback response appropriate for the current physical state, along with the sensing, drive energy, braking, and holding premises required to execute it safely. For manual teleoperation, the reference design chooses a `{python} InterventionTimeoutBudget.manual_lease_str` lease, bounded from below by heartbeat loss and jitter and from above by the clearance its extra travel over the chunk lease consumes after the takeover.
* **Clearance governs waiting:** A takeover delay is travel before braking, so its allowance comes from the stopping budget, not from a configured timer. The subtotal before dispatch-to-admission travel allows `{python} InterventionSummaryWaiting.t_latest_str` of waiting at the aisle speed, `{python} InterventionAdmissionAllocation.left_aisle_str` once the `{python} InterventionAdmissionAllocation.delta_da_str` admission allocation is charged, and `{python} InterventionSummaryWaiting.t_latest_in_str` at the `{python} InterventionSummaryWaiting.v_in_str` slow-down, which still leaves `{python} InterventionAdmissionAllocation.left_in_da_str` after an in-loop takeover and the charge. Price human responses at design percentiles, not averages. The `{python} InterventionSummaryWaiting.t_in_str` in-loop design response caps the request speed at `{python} InterventionSummaryWaiting.ceil_in_str` and the `{python} InterventionSummaryWaiting.t_ool_str` out-of-loop response caps it at `{python} InterventionSummaryWaiting.ceil_ool_str`. Dispatch the fallback at the earliest of the protocol, lease, evidence, and clearance deadlines, and stop before handing an unexpected hazard to an out-of-loop operator.
* **Single-writer actuator ownership:** Explicit source arbitration and exclusive enforcer command ownership eliminate conflicting actuator writes; low-level bus arbitration alone cannot establish safety authority. Every request, commit, and confirmation message must explicitly declare its channel mask. A partial transfer, such as reassigning arm control while the base keeps navigating autonomously, is admissible only while the console annunciates the untransferred channel's owner; otherwise that channel holds. A four-phase protocol (Request, Acknowledge, Commit, Confirm) transitions authority deterministically. The commit transition revokes the autonomous policy token on the designated channels and latches its last admitted command. No proposer holds the proposal token during `BLEND`, while the enforcer owns the command; the arbiter grants the token to the operator only after the profile completes, and the enforcer then checks human proposals against the same physical envelopes as the policy's.
* **Smooth command blending and haptic passivity:** A fixed-endpoint $\Glyph{C}^2$ acceleration profile bounds peak jerk during authority transitions, and its additional stopping displacement must be reserved in the braking envelope. If the system incorporates bilateral force reflection, the console feedback loop requires its own passivity and stability argument evaluated under realistic network latency, packet loss, and actuator dynamics.
* **Independent stopping paths:** Dedicated, hardwired protective circuits execute risk-assessed mechanical and electrical stops independent of software. Network-delivered commands undergo cryptographic admission checks: corrupted or unauthenticated packets are dropped at ingress, whereas a failure to refresh a valid lease triggers an autonomous local fallback.
* **Causal data attribution:** Training on intervention logs requires preserving controller provenance and declaring target and eligibility rules. This chapter's conservative direct-imitation mask $\CausalInterventionMask(\TimeInstant)$ (@eq-intervention-causal-masking-loss) preserves learner-visited drift states for failure analysis and automated relabeling, zeros out synthetic enforcer blending splines ($\BlendingTransitionWindow$) and initial operator hunting, and admits only validated, stabilized human recovery as post-takeover demonstration targets. Other objectives may retain or weight early corrections differently (@tbl-14-intervention-learning).
* **Authority as auditable evidence:** The authority record logs per-tick evidence tuples $\langle \MicrocontrollerClockTime, \RecordedAuthorityState, \MechanicalPlantState, \NominalControlCommand, \CertifiedControlAction, \JointTorque, \text{ID}_{\text{operator}}, \RemainingExecutionLease\rangle$ into tamper-evident cryptographic hash chains, treating a missing entry as an explicit fault rather than an implied pass. The manifest's four authority rules serve as primary test targets for verification fault injection; their passing logs, anchored by the authority record, are the evidence the release argument needs before it may admit remote takeover.
:::

A person's authority over an embodied physical AI system is granted on verifiable evidence and expires when that evidence lapses, as the fourth law, permission must be earned (principle \ref{pri-vol4-evidence-bounds-authority}), requires of every privilege the machine honors. Fresh credentials, checked plant state, a feasible target and fallback reserve, and a successfully committed handshake support the grant of authority; the manual lease bounds how long the grant remains valid while its physical premises continue to hold. When operator inputs cease renewing the lease, authority immediately lapses to a verified local fallback governed by the hardware permission path. Preemption tiers do not persist across a lease expiration: a remote assistant who previously commanded the mobile base retains no residual authority once the lease expires. Re-establishing control under any proposer requires satisfying the reset conditions of the authority state machine and presenting fresh, validated credentials.

## Historical Perspective and Further Reading {#sec-intervention-history}

Supervisory control emerged as an engineering discipline when teleoperated systems outgrew direct manual control. In deep-sea exploration and hazardous environment manipulation, transmission latency and high operator workloads made continuous teleoperation fragile. @sheridan1978human formalized the division of labor between human operators and machine intelligence, grading autonomy into explicit levels that range from complete manual execution to autonomous computer execution that ignores human input. @sheridan1992telerobotics consolidated these insights into a unified systems theory of human supervisory control, modeling how human operators alternate between planning, programming, monitoring, intervening, and learning from automated subroutines. Expanding on this taxonomy, @parasuraman2000model decoupled automation across four functional dimensions: sensory information acquisition, information analysis, decision selection, and action execution, assigning distinct operational levels to each stage. Meanwhile, industrial process automation approached supervisory handovers from a control-theoretic perspective. Switching a closed-loop plant between manual operation and automatic tracking without inducing mechanical shock or actuator saturation requires the idle controller to track the active plant state continuously. This bumpless transfer technique, detailed as standard practice by @astrom2006advanced, provides the classical foundation that this chapter's enforcer generalizes: smoothly blending between verified endpoint states while strictly respecting physical actuator limits.

Human factors engineering revealed why relying on a passive human operator as an emergency fallback is fundamentally flawed. In a landmark critique, @bainbridge1983ironies articulated the central irony of automation: automating routine operations leaves the human supervisor responsible solely for rare, anomalous edge cases, precisely when sustained inactivity has degraded both situational awareness and manual control proficiency. @sarter1995mode examined cockpit automation to trace the root causes of mode confusion, demonstrating how silent automation state changes lead pilots to issue inputs that are entirely correct for their assumed operational mode but hazardous for the aircraft's actual mode. @endsley1995toward formalized the cognitive basis of operator intervention, decomposing situation awareness into three hierarchical tiers: perceiving sensory cues, comprehending the operational state, and projecting system trajectories into the near future. Physical latency imposes strict mathematical limits on these interactions. @ferrell1965remote demonstrated that when loop delays exceed a fraction of a second, human operators inevitably degrade into a disjointed "move-and-wait" strategy to avoid destabilizing the physical plant. In bilateral teleoperation with force reflection, delayed feedback injects non-physical energy into the loop and can destabilize it. @anderson1989bilateral addressed this instability through a passive communication-channel construction within a specified bilateral control architecture. Closed-loop stability also depends on the channel terminations and the coupled controllers and plant. @niemeyer1991stable reformulated the communication-channel passivity condition using wave variables. Variable delay, packet loss, sampling, and saturation require the additional analysis identified in @sec-appendix-control-passivity. At the architectural level, arbitrating between competing subsystem commands using rigid priorities directly descends from the layered suppression and inhibition mechanisms pioneered by @brooks1986robust in the subsumption architecture.

Machine learning turned supervisory intervention into a source of training data. @ross2011reduction proved that naive behavioral cloning fails under distributional drift because the autonomous policy inevitably encounters states absent from the expert demonstrations; robust training requires querying the expert along the learner's own induced state distribution via the DAgger algorithm. To reduce human fatigue, @kelly2019hgdagger introduced Human-Gated DAgger, delegating continuous control to the autonomous policy and recording demonstrations only when the human supervisor actively intervenes. Modern embodied systems generalize these intervention boundaries into core training signals: Sirius [@liu2023sirius] uses intervention transitions as prioritized sample weights in offline policy optimization, @luo2024rlif converts supervisory takeovers into reinforcement learning reward penalties, and @luo2025hilserl uses intervention corrections to drive real-world robotic reinforcement learning safely on physical hardware. Every data-driven approach relies on unambiguous execution provenance: the system must record exactly which agent (human supervisor, machine policy, or safety enforcer) held authority over every actuator command. Tamper-evident logging draws on a deep cryptographic lineage, from the cryptographically linked timestamps of @haber1991time to the hierarchical authentication structures of @merkle1988digital. This chapter integrates these disparate systems threads into a single runtime abstraction: a per-tick authority record that aligns the handover sequence with the physical stopping budget and retains ownership boundaries for downstream policy learning. The arbiter and enforcer establish exclusive channel ownership; per-channel announcements support mode awareness, and the record supports evaluating both under its timing and capture assumptions.

Six works trace this lineage from the ironies of automation to learning from interventions:

- @bainbridge1983ironies articulates why automating routine operations deprives human operators of the running mental model and manual dexterity required to handle anomalous edge cases, establishing the engineering motivation for executing a safe dynamic stop before requesting intervention.
- @sheridan1992telerobotics provides the definitive monograph uniting supervisory control, teleoperation architectures, and the dynamics of delayed human-in-the-loop systems.
- @sarter1995mode identifies the cognitive mechanics of mode awareness breakdowns in complex cockpits, illustrating the failure modes that per-channel masks and state announcements mitigate in @sec-intervention-failure-modes.
- @parasuraman2000model establishes the multi-dimensional taxonomy of automation across acquisition, analysis, decision, and action, providing the conceptual architecture behind channel-by-channel capability matrices.
- @anderson1989bilateral develops a passive communication-channel construction for delayed bilateral teleoperation, forming the analytical basis for @sec-intervention-haptic-passivity. Its closed-loop stability argument depends on the specified channel terminations and control architecture.
- @ross2011reduction introduces the DAgger algorithm and demonstrates that imitation learners must be trained against corrections collected on their own visited state distributions, explaining why the authority record must capture policy drift intervals and takeover boundaries.

::: {.callout-chapter-connection title="From authority revocation to verification"}
Operational logs alone cannot establish that the arbiter enforces its rules under adverse conditions. Weeks of clean handovers in the authority record rarely contain a duplicate writer, a replayed packet, or a dropped heartbeat, and a record cannot testify about a fault that never occurred. The same gap runs through every record this book has developed, because the chunk lease, the permission path, and the held-up permission rail all describe protective responses that normal operation never exercises. @Sec-verification creates those faults on purpose. It pairs four physical faults injected as the loaded base approaches the rack end, beginning with a stalled proposer, with the four authority rules A1 through A4 that this chapter's manifest hands over, and it scores each trial against an oracle fixed before the test, measured by instruments the fault cannot reach rather than by the arbiter's own account of what it did.
:::
